* First, let's open some libraries that we'll be using
```{r message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(caTools)
library(tm)
library(mlapi)
library(e1071)
library(caret)
```

* Next, we have to load the dataset
```{r}
full_training_set <- read.csv('train.csv')
glimpse(full_training_set)
```


* Now let's load the text and preprocess it based on our knowledge from the last few classes
```{r}
all_training_texts <-full_training_set$text
all_training_texts_corpus <- VCorpus(VectorSource(all_training_texts))
all_training_texts_corpus <- tm_map(all_training_texts_corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
all_training_texts_corpus <- tm_map(all_training_texts_corpus, removePunctuation)
all_training_texts_corpus <- tm_map(all_training_texts_corpus, removeWords,stopwords("english"))
all_training_texts_corpus <- tm_map(all_training_texts_corpus, stemDocument)
length(all_training_texts_corpus)

```
* Now that we've loaded and preprocessed the texts, let's start vectorizing! *But we will split the training and test sets first to avoid data leak*. 
* First, let's generate n-grams by defining a function called NLP_tokenizer. Then we convert all the tweets into n-grams (1-3). If you study the code carefully, you'll see that for 2- and 3-grams, adjacent words are being concatenated using an *underscore* character.
```{r}
NLP_tokenizer <- function(x) {
  unlist(lapply(ngrams(words(x), 1:3), paste, collapse = "_"), use.names = FALSE)
}
training_n_gram_corpus <- tm_map(all_training_texts_corpus,content_transformer(NLP_tokenizer))
```

* We can view the length of the corpus and the content to ensure that the n-grams were generated appropriately.
```{r}
length(training_n_gram_corpus)
training_n_gram_corpus[[4]]$content
```

* Now we split the sets (before vectorizing them). We also split the classes in the same manner.
```{r}
set.seed(1234)
split <- sample.split(full_training_set$label,SplitRatio = 0.8)
training_ngram_subset <- subset(training_n_gram_corpus, split==TRUE)
evaluation_ngram_subset <- subset(training_n_gram_corpus, split==FALSE)
training_subset_classes <- subset(full_training_set$label, split==TRUE)
evalutation_subset_classes <- subset(full_training_set$label, split==FALSE)

#creating another set from the training set for hyperparameter optimization
split <- sample.split(training_subset_classes,SplitRatio = 0.8)
training_hp_subset <- subset(training_ngram_subset, split==TRUE)
training_hp_classes <- subset(training_subset_classes, split==TRUE)
validation_ngram_subset <- subset(training_ngram_subset, split==FALSE)
validation_ngram_classes <- subset(training_subset_classes,split==FALSE)
```

* Now that we have separated the sets, we can start vectorizing. We are doing it step by step. First, we are generating a document-term matrix for the training set. Then we are removing sparse n-grams.
```{r}
training_dct_matrix <- DocumentTermMatrix(training_hp_subset)
training_dct_matrix_sparse <- removeSparseTerms(training_dct_matrix,0.995)
```

* Now we are vectorizing the validation set..
```{r}
val_dct_matrix_sparse <- DocumentTermMatrix(validation_ngram_subset, list(dictionary=colnames(training_dct_matrix_sparse)))
```
* The next steps are straightforward. We convert to data frames and make sure the instances follow the R-specific formats.
```{r}
training_term_matrix_df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(training_dct_matrix_sparse))
val_term_matrix_df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(val_dct_matrix_sparse))
colnames(training_term_matrix_df) <- make.names(colnames(training_term_matrix_df))
colnames(val_term_matrix_df) <- make.names(colnames(val_dct_matrix_sparse))
training_term_matrix_df$label <- training_hp_classes
training_term_matrix_df$label <-as.factor(training_term_matrix_df$label)
```

* Here, we are experimenting with different values of the cost parameter
```{r}
i = 1
while  (i <= 64){ 
  trained_model <- svm(label ~., data=training_term_matrix_df,cost=i)
  predictions <- predict(trained_model,newdata=val_term_matrix_df)
  #print(i)
  print(confusionMatrix(as.factor(validation_ngram_classes),predictions))
  i = i*2
}
```
* Now, we will perform the final evaluation on the held-out test set (training on the entire training set data)
```{r}
training_dct_matrix <- DocumentTermMatrix(training_ngram_subset)
training_dct_matrix_sparse <- removeSparseTerms(training_dct_matrix,0.995)

eval_dct_matrix_sparse <- DocumentTermMatrix(evaluation_ngram_subset, list(dictionary=colnames(training_dct_matrix_sparse)))

training_term_matrix_df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(training_dct_matrix_sparse))
eval_term_matrix_df <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(eval_dct_matrix_sparse))
colnames(training_term_matrix_df) <- make.names(colnames(training_term_matrix_df))
colnames(eval_term_matrix_df) <- make.names(colnames(eval_dct_matrix_sparse))
training_term_matrix_df$label <- training_subset_classes
training_term_matrix_df$label <-as.factor(training_term_matrix_df$label)

trained_model <- svm(label ~., data=training_term_matrix_df,cost=2)
predictions <- predict(trained_model, newdata=eval_term_matrix_df)
print(confusionMatrix(as.factor(evalutation_subset_classes),predictions))
```
